title: A bare position carries no prior occurrences: the repeated position of mx-chs-004 supplied with no history is ongoing
rationale: This start_fen is byte-identical to the result_fen of mx-chs-004, which the contract rules a loss for the chasing side at the third occurrence. Here the same position record is supplied bare: the a3 chariot does attack the unprotected a5 horse, so the chase threat is standing on the board, and the position is still ongoing. A perpetual chase is a single behaviour sustained across three occurrences of a position, and a bare position carries no prior occurrences, so one standing threat is not a violation. This is the sharp form of the rule: what makes a chase perpetual is the supplied history, never the attack visible in the position.
